paper.title_en: Stringent Constraints on Spin-Spin-Velocity-Dependent Exotic Interactions with a Levitated Magnet Force Sensor
paper.abstract_en: Exotic spin-spin-velocity-dependent interactions, predicted in extensions of the standard model involving new bosonic fields, could resolve fundamental puzzles from dark matter to cosmic asymmetry. However, exploring these weak potential interactions at centimeter scales presents formidable challenges, primarily due to the overwhelming dominance of electromagnetic backgrounds that can easily obscure the weak exotic signals. Here, we utilize a levitated magnet force sensor with ultrahigh electron spin density to probe these interactions. We constrain two interactions individually through a designed spin source and a multilayer magnetic shielding system that suppresses electromagnetic backgrounds. In this Letter, we constrain two types of interactions: the <math display="inline"><msub><mi>V</mi><mn>6</mn></msub></math> potential at force ranges from <math display="inline"><mrow><msup><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> to <math display="inline"><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mtext> </mtext><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow></math> and the <math display="inline"><msub><mi>V</mi><mn>14</mn></msub></math> potential at ranges greater than <math display="inline"><mrow><msup><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mtext> </mtext><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow></math>. Our measurements establish 95% confidence-level bounds of <math display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>6</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mo>≤</mo><mn>2.12</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>13</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> and <math display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>14</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mo>≤</mo><mn>2.34</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>23</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> at <math display="inline"><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1.6</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mtext> </mtext><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow></math>, improving prior limits by up to 12 and 13 orders of magnitude, respectively. Our result demonstrates the levitated magnet as a highly sensitive probe for detecting new bosonic fields in extensions of the standard model.
